history.heading: The Tongan Empire
paragraphs: Tonga, an archipelago of about 170 islands in the South Pacific, was settled around 3,000 years ago by the Lapita people. From around the 10th century, the Tu'i Tonga dynasty built a maritime chiefdom that extended influence over Samoa, Fiji and other islands, sometimes called the Tongan Empire. The Ha'amonga 'a Maui trilithon is an ancient stone monument.
Captain Cook visited in the 1770s and named Tonga the "Friendly Islands". After civil wars, King George Tupou I unified Tonga in 1845, adopted Christianity and introduced a constitution in 1875.

history.heading: A kingdom never colonised
paragraphs: Tonga became a British protected state in 1900 but kept its monarchy and was never formally colonised. It regained full independence in 1970. Riots in 2006 led to democratic reforms in 2010. In January 2022 the Hunga Tonga–Hunga Ha'apai volcano erupted in one of the largest explosions ever recorded, causing a tsunami.

culture.heading: Tongan traditions
paragraphs: Tongan and English are official languages. Christianity, especially Methodism, is central, and Sunday is strictly observed; most activities are banned. Traditional values of respect, family and rank remain strong.
The ta'ovala, a woven mat worn around the waist, is formal dress. Tapa cloth, made from bark, is a prized craft. Rugby is a passion, and Tongan players are prominent internationally.

politics.heading: Constitutional monarchy
paragraphs: Tonga is a constitutional monarchy; King Tupou VI is head of state. Since the 2010 reforms, most members of the Legislative Assembly are elected by the people, with some seats reserved for nobles, and parliament elects the prime minister. The king retains significant powers.

economy.heading: Remittances
paragraphs: Tonga's economy depends heavily on remittances from Tongans living in New Zealand, Australia and the US, among the highest shares of GDP in the world. Agriculture (squash, vanilla and root crops), fishing and tourism are also important. Tonga has significant debt to China. The currency is the pa'anga.
